small_guidance:
- The softmax_sigmoid kernel is fine but cheap; the real cost is ConvTranspose3d. Tuning the softmax (num_warps=4, BLOCK_C=64) will only shave microseconds. Don't spend cycles here.
- If kept, autotune over `num_warps ∈ {2,4,8}` keyed on C; BLOCK_C=64 (next-pow2 of 64) with num_warps=4 should be near-optimal already.
- Ensure the output of conv_transpose is already contiguous (it is) and avoid the extra `.contiguous()` call when unnecessary.
large_guidance:
- Replace ConvTranspose3d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and atomically scattering into output positions `(d*stride - pad + kd, ...)`. Handle output_padding via output shape. Fuse bias add into the same kernel as initialization (write bias to output once, then atomic_add contributions).
- Alternatively, implement as a gather-based GEMM: for each output position, gather the valid input positions and weights into a (OC, IC*KD*KH*KW) × (IC*KD*KH*KW, tile) matmul. Tile (BLOCK_M=32, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=16), num_warps=4, num_stages=2 to fit SMEM. Use channels-last layout so IC is contiguous in the K reduction.
- Fuse the softmax+sigmoid epilogue into the conv-transpose kernel only if the conv kernel is persistent per (N, spatial) so the full channel axis is reduced in-register. Otherwise keep softmax_sigmoid as a separate (already-fast) post-pass.
